title: One act at your own scale
line: This week, one thing for your street, building or town.
intro: For the Greeks, as Athena reads them, we are political by nature, so “I’m not political” is itself a political stance. Politics starts at your own scale: your street, your building, your town, wherever people reason together. This week you do one act there, and report it in two lines.
does: Do one act this week for your street, building or town, and report it in two lines.
trains: Taking up your political nature at the scale you can reach.
steps: Choose one thing that would make your street, building, village or community a little better and that you can do yourself this week: tidy a shared space, help a neighbour, go to a residents’ or town meeting, start a conversation about something you share.
If you can, leave room for others to reason with you: ask a neighbour what they think, or invite someone along.
report: What did you do, and for whom?
What did you notice in yourself as a citizen, a πολίτης, while you did it?
